sections.content: A pesar de introduces a contrast the writer chooses not to let win — a fact stands despite an obstacle. A raíz de introduces a cause: something happened as a direct result of an earlier event. Historians reach for both constantly, because weighing evidence almost always means admitting a contradiction (a pesar de) or tracing a consequence (a raíz de). These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: A pesar de que los mayas escribían con un sistema jeroglífico completo, hoy solo sobreviven cuatro libros mayas originales.
items.english: Despite the fact that the Maya wrote with a complete hieroglyphic system, today only four original Maya books survive.

items.spanish: A raíz de ese acto, y de otras destrucciones similares durante la conquista, casi toda la literatura maya escrita desapareció para siempre.
items.english: As a result of that act, and other similar destructions during the conquest, almost all written Maya literature disappeared forever.

items.spanish: A pesar de las lagunas y las pérdidas, cada fuente aporta una pieza distinta.
items.english: Despite the gaps and the losses, each source contributes a distinct piece.

items.spanish: A raíz de descubrimientos recientes, la imagen del mundo precolombino sigue cambiando.
items.english: As a result of recent discoveries, the picture of the pre-Columbian world keeps changing.

sections.content: Both connectors take a noun or a full clause with *que*: *a pesar de + [noun / que + clause]*, *a raíz de + [noun]*. Don't confuse a pesar de (despite, a contrast) with a causa de (because of, a plain cause) — a raíz de sits between the two: a cause with a sense of "and everything changed after."
